ctoNEAR. So `formatNear(1)` has to show `0.00` or some other two-decimal value, and `parseNear` of any such string is a multiple of `10^22`. It can never return `1`. The same holds for any amount with nonzero digits beyond the second decimal place. No patch to `formatNear` can satisfy both rules.

`bun test` currently gives 1 pass and 2 fail. The two failures are the trailing-zero bug (`1.5` instead of `1.50`, `2` instead of `2.00`). The fix for those alone is easy, but it would still break the round-trip rule for amounts finer than 0.01 NEAR, so a hidden test on that rule would fail.
